summary: The current tenant handler only dispatches on slug presence, while existing query construction, PBAC, child-owner resolution, and schema compatibility each introduce risks for the proposed peek-and-thread design. The highest-risk gaps are authorization ordering, child tenant overrides, dry-run isolation, and rollout compatibility for the new column.

suggestions.title: Preserve authorization-before-definition lookup
suggestions.rationale: QueryService currently performs `_enforce_owned_slug` before `get_source()` and its repository lookup. A tenant dispatcher that calls `repo.get()` first can expose existence timing/errors or perform database work for unauthorized slugs. Build the identity from the resolved store, authorize before loading, and add a regression proving unauthorized existing and missing slugs have identical behavior and do not preload definitions.

suggestions.title: Centralize tenant load, error mapping, and dispatch
suggestions.rationale: `query()`, `columns()`, and `test_slug()` currently repeat store validation and request setup, while `TenantError` mapping is distributed across delegates. Add one tenant-specific loader/dispatcher that resolves the identity, preserves existing HTTP error envelopes, stores the loaded definition, and selects the handler. Assert exactly one `DefinitionRepository.get()` call per top-level route.

suggestions.title: Thread the definition through the shared query base explicitly
suggestions.rationale: `QS` and `MultiQS` currently accept arbitrary `**kwargs`, which flow through `BaseQuery`, `AbstractQuery`, and `Connection`; an unhandled `definition` keyword would be silently ignored. Store and validate it in the shared query state, then pass it through `AbstractHandler.get_source()` and all four `QueryService` construction sites. Preserve the default `None` path for legacy callers.

suggestions.title: Resolve child PBAC against each child owner
suggestions.rationale: `QueryHandler._preflight_multiquery_owned()` currently checks every child slug against `request['qs_tenant']`, but `MultiQS.query()` resolves explicit child `tenant` values and passes different stores to execution. A child explicitly moved to another tenant can therefore be authorized against the parent store while executing from the child store. Make the ownership preflight consume resolved `(slug, store)` identities and test inheritance, explicit tenant, and explicit null override cases.

suggestions.title: Implement dry-run validation as a pure multi-definition phase
suggestions.rationale: The existing multi path deep-copies configuration, performs repository preflight, constructs `ThreadQuery`, and executes sources; the single dry-run also issues `EXPLAIN ANALYZE`. A validate-only path should share a pure child-resolution/preflight helper with execution, return deterministic per-child statuses, and never construct executors, open datasource connections, or call `EXPLAIN`.

suggestions.title: Handle multi columns directly instead of delegating to the legacy empty response
suggestions.rationale: `QueryHandler.columns()` always returns 204 with `No Columns available` and has no stored-slug or definition input. The tenant handler must return the declared `columns_definition` for non-empty multi definitions, preserve the exact empty 204 headers, and apply the intended ownership check before revealing the declaration. Add separate HEAD and PATCH response tests.

suggestions.title: Define a migration or old-store write policy for columns_definition
suggestions.rationale: Registry compatibility currently requires only `query_slug`, and the existing tenant DDL fixtures omit the new column. `DefinitionRepository.create()` and `upsert()` serialize the validated model dynamically, so a defaulted `columns_definition` can be included in writes to an old table and fail at runtime. Either require and verify a migration before registration, or omit the field for stores whose `QueryStore.columns` lacks it; explicitly decide whether `public.queries` is writable-compatible.

suggestions.title: Add exact single-parity and no-double-read contract tests
suggestions.rationale: Current HTTP tests verify only slug-presence dispatch and do not inspect the loaded definition. Add tests that capture the definition passed to `QS`/`MultiQS`, assert one repository read, verify identity/revision propagation, and compare tenant single-slug headers, cache inputs, status mapping, download/filename handling, queryformat, and `X-Slug` with the existing service behavior.

suggestions.title: Use the opt-in integration suite for schema and stored-multi coverage
suggestions.rationale: The repository already has isolated PostgreSQL/Redis fixtures, but their DDL and integration rows currently cover ordinary definitions rather than a stored `provider='multi'` pipeline. Add an opt-in route test with a real multi row, declared columns, child inheritance/overrides, and revision/cache assertions; keep unit tests for no-datasource dry-run guarantees.

suggestions.title: Consider rejecting malformed provider=multi payloads on tenant routes
suggestions.rationale: `MultiQS` currently falls back from a non-multi `query_raw` to a synthetic single child, which can trigger another definition load and makes the provider discriminator less deterministic. The scheduler already identifies `provider='multi'` and logs malformed payloads. A tenant-only 422 for malformed multi payloads would simplify no-double-read guarantees; if compatibility requires fallback, explicitly pass the already loaded runtime into the synthetic child path and test its read count.
